questions.q: What does the AWS Glue Data Catalog store?
options: Your Parquet and CSV files themselves
Trained model artifacts
Metadata about your data, such as location, schema and properties
Query results from Athena only
questions.explain: The Data Catalog is a metadata repository organized into databases and tables. The data stays in S3; a table entry records where it is and what columns it has.

questions.q: Why is it useful for a data scientist that the catalog is shared across services?
options: Every notebook must hard-code its own file paths
Athena, Glue jobs and other tools see the same table name and schema
It automatically trains models on new data
It removes the need for IAM permissions
questions.explain: Athena, Redshift Spectrum, EMR, Glue jobs and SageMaker AI integrate with the same catalog, so a table is defined once. Access still needs IAM permissions.

questions.q: Which are the Glue job types named in the AWS documentation used in this lesson?
options: Spark, Spark Streaming and Python shell
Only Spark
Notebook, Lambda and Fargate
Batch, Real-time and Serverless
questions.explain: The Glue job properties documentation lists Spark, Spark Streaming and Python shell. Check the current docs, since offerings change.

questions.q: In a Glue script, what does dyf.toDF() do?
options: Deletes the table from the catalog
Writes the data to Parquet
Starts a crawler
Converts a DynamicFrame into a Spark DataFrame
questions.explain: A DynamicFrame is Glue's data structure. toDF() converts it to a Spark DataFrame so you can use ordinary Spark transformations.

questions.q: According to the lesson, when is a notebook with pandas the right place to prepare features?
options: For prototyping on data that fits in memory
For scheduled preparation of terabytes
Never, since Glue is always required
Only after Redshift has loaded the data
questions.explain: Prototype the logic in pandas on a sample. Move to a Glue Spark job when the work must be repeatable and large scale.
